open_points.subject: confirmation binding in A13 rule 6, Required test 12 and A21's review
open_points.text:
A pending confirmation shown for one action, target, version and inputs
    is refused, and used up, when the submission carrying its value changes
    any one of them: another action, another target, another version or
    none, another value of any input, or the same list in another order
    (rule 6).
open_points.question: Must every changed tuple be refused, as Required test 12 and A21 say, or may a changed tuple be treated as bound when its encoding has a digest collision, as rule 6 permits by placing collisions outside the guarantee?
options: Qualify the refusal guarantee: a changed tuple is refused when its digest differs, while collisions remain outside the guarantee.
Keep the absolute refusal guarantee and retain enough collision-disambiguating information to compare the submitted tuple after a digest match.
Keep only a digest but make collision-freedom an absolute product guarantee, replacing the stated collision-resistance limit.
open_points.default_guess: Qualify Required test 12 and A21's claim to the digest comparison actually guaranteed, because rule 6 expressly excludes digest collisions and excludes retaining the values.

witness.initial: A session has a valid pending confirmation for tuple T, and a different admissible tuple T2 has a different unambiguous encoding but the same digest.
events: The owner submits T2 with the pending confirmation value before it expires, passing the session and CSRF checks.
Registry compares the stored digest with the digest of T2.
outcomes: Under rule 6, the digests are equal, so T2 is bound and the otherwise valid action may be accepted.
Under Required test 12 and A21's statement that changing any component is refused, the submission is refused and the pending confirmation is used up.
witness.observer: The owner observes refusal versus acceptance, and the store may show the action's state change.

open_points.subject: verification of OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS coverage
open_points.text:
The table has exactly one
   row for each owner action M09 lists, for each transition and each erasure
   kind it has — the erasure of old entries among them (A15 rule 6) — and no
   other
open_points.question: Which later check proves that the imported table has every required row exactly once and no extra row, including every transition and project-erasure kind?
options: Compare the constant's complete key set with a generated expected set derived from the declared owner actions, transitions and erasure kinds.
Use a parameterized behavioral test for every required action and a separate assertion that the table has no extra keys.
Rely only on the behavioral action tests.
open_points.default_guess: Compare the complete table key set with the generated expected set and also retain behavioral tests for the resulting audit entries.
consequences: Complete-set comparison proves missing, duplicate and extra-row constraints directly.
Parameterized tests can prove behavior and no-extra-key structure but require careful enumeration of every discriminator.
Behavioral tests alone may miss unused extra rows and therefore do not establish the stated exactness constraint.
open_points.requirement:
The table has exactly one
   row for each owner action M09 lists, for each transition and each erasure
   kind it has — the erasure of old entries among them (A15 rule 6) — and no
   other

set_aside.subject: cryptographic digest algorithm for pending-confirmation bindings
set_aside.text: The digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest
set_aside.question: Which concrete digest algorithm and output size must generated code use?
set_aside.default_guess: Use SHA-256 through one internal hashing utility.
consequences: SHA-256 is broadly available and easy for Factory checks to recognize, but fixes that primitive in generated code.
SHA-512/256 provides a different implementation and availability profile while preserving a 256-bit result.
BLAKE2b-256 is efficient and supports personalization, but introduces different library/API expectations.
set_aside.requirement: The digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: encoding of confirmation action, target, version and inputs
set_aside.text:
one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs
   in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from
   an empty one
set_aside.question: What exact serialization or framing does generated code use to make the tuple encoding injective across value types, field boundaries, absent values, empty values and ordered lists?
options: Canonical JSON with an explicit typed envelope and explicit absent markers.
Canonical CBOR with fixed schema tags.
set_aside.default_guess: Use a type-tagged, length-prefixed binary encoding with explicit markers for absent values, sequences and scalar types.
consequences: Length-prefixing makes boundaries and type distinctions direct but requires a dedicated encoder.
Canonical JSON is readily inspectable but needs strict rules for Unicode, numbers, object keys and absent values.
Canonical CBOR is compact and standardized but adds encoder and canonicalization dependencies.
set_aside.requirement:
The digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one
   unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs
   in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from
   an empty one, so that two different tuples never share an encoding; that
   two encodings share a digest is outside the guarantee.
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: Factory evidence for the new digest and encoding guarantees
set_aside.text:
The digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one
   unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs
   in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from
   an empty one, so that two different tuples never share an encoding
set_aside.question: Which Factory checks establish use of an approved collision-resistant primitive and the required encoding distinctions, since Required test 12 only exercises selected changed inputs?
options: A static code check for an approved digest primitive plus property tests over the tuple encoder.
Only behavioral examples corresponding to Required test 12.
A generated encoder review/check against a declared serialization schema plus behavioral tests.
set_aside.default_guess: Use an approved-primitive static check and property-based tests for type, boundary, absence, emptiness and list-order distinctions.
consequences: Static checking plus property tests directly covers both hidden implementation properties but requires a dedicated Factory rule.
Behavioral examples are simpler but do not establish the general injectivity or primitive requirement.
A declared serialization schema gives strong reproducibility but adds a schema artifact and a conformance check.
